question: Past 32K, can these models find and use information in a long context on one RTX 3090 24GB, and how fast do they answer?

qwen36_35b_a3b.note: pin repo, revision, SHA-256 and verify chat template in Phase 0

length_rule: size each document so every model's tokenized prompt (document + question + chat template) stays at least 2,048 tokens under ctx_size; record actual per-model token counts
fit_fallback: if a model cannot load ctx_size fully on GPU, record it as not fitting and test that model's long_128k documents truncated to the largest multiple of 8192 it loads; label clearly

generation.sampling: each model's recommended settings, recorded in DATA/sampling.json
generation.seed_rule: fixed seed per question, identical across models

answer_format: single short JSON object per question
scoring: deterministic exact match after case/whitespace normalization; multi_retrieval uses set equality; no model judge; every question has a reference answer and a negative control the scorer must reject
prompt_cache: document prefix processed once per document per model; cache reuse verified per request from llama.cpp prompt-token counts
haystack: public-domain long-form text with synthetic facts inserted at recorded positions; source and license cited
cost_rule: actual running GPU-hours x RunPod advertised RTX 3090 list price; estimate, not invoice
position_rule: single_retrieval nominal bands early ≈ first third, middle ≈ second third, late ≈ last third; actual planted character fractions published per question in fact_fractions. Other facts spread across 5–95%.
budget_checkpoint: after the first model finishes all lengths, project the total from measured generated tokens and speeds; if the projection exceeds the hard stop, stop and report before starting the next model
dataset_rules: answer values are random strings with no shared number, word or pattern with the question key (no ID-number echo)
entity names are randomized, not sequential (no -001, -002 numbering)
facts are written as plain sentences that fit the surrounding prose; no "synthetic", "record" or other marker labels
near-miss distractor facts (same entity type, different entity) are planted so retrieval requires matching the exact entity
aggregation counts vary between 2 and 8, with distractor occurrences of other markers
multi-hop chains use randomized names at each hop, placed at different positions
